role_sought: City councillor, Madrid (23rd on the PSOE list led by Trinidad Jiménez)
result: Not elected (entered the council in May 2004 as a replacement)
detail: The PSOE won 21 seats, so 23rd place on the list did not secure a seat; he took up a vacancy on the council on 18 May 2004.
Re-elected to the council in opposition; served until 15 September 2009, when he entered Congress.

role_sought: Member of the Congress of Deputies for Madrid (PSOE list)
result: Not elected (entered Congress in September 2009 as a replacement)
detail: Not in an electable position; took the seat vacated by Pedro Solbes on 15 September 2009.

role_sought: Member of the Congress of Deputies for Madrid (11th on the PSOE list)
result: Not elected (entered Congress in January 2013 as a replacement)
detail: Lost his seat in the PSOE's 2011 defeat; returned on 10 January 2013 to fill the vacancy left by Cristina Narbona.

opponent: Eduardo Madina (c. 36%), José Antonio Pérez Tapias (c. 15%)
detail: First PSOE leadership vote open to all party members; confirmed as Secretary-General at the extraordinary congress of 26 July 2014.

role_sought: President of the Government (PSOE candidate; head of the Madrid list)
result: PSOE second (90 seats); elected deputy; investiture failed
detail: After a coalition agreement with Ciudadanos, his investiture bid was defeated in Congress on 2 and 4 March 2016, leading to a repeat election.

role_sought: President of the Government (PSOE candidate; head of the Madrid list)
detail: Opposed abstaining to allow Rajoy's investiture; resigned as PSOE leader on 1 October 2016 and gave up his seat on 29 October 2016.
Returned to the party leadership against the candidate backed by much of the party establishment; took office again on 17 June 2017.

election: Motion of no confidence against Mariano Rajoy (Congress of Deputies)
role_sought: President of the Government (candidate named in the constructive motion)
result: Motion carried; became President of the Government
detail: Tabled by the PSOE after the Audiencia Nacional's Gürtel judgment; supported by Unidos Podemos and Basque and Catalan nationalist and pro-independence parties. First successful motion of no confidence in Spanish democracy.

role_sought: President of the Government (PSOE candidate; head of the Madrid list)
result: PSOE first (123 seats); elected deputy; investiture failed in July 2019
detail: The PSOE's first general-election win since 2008, short of a majority. Talks with Unidas Podemos failed and his July 2019 investiture bid was rejected, leading to a repeat election.

role_sought: President of the Government (PSOE candidate; head of the Madrid list)
result: PSOE first (120 seats); elected deputy; invested on 7 January 2020
vote_share: 28.0% (PSOE, Congress); investiture: 167 in favour, 165 against, 18 abstentions
detail: Formed a coalition government with Unidas Podemos, the first coalition government of the current democratic period; elected on the second (simple-majority) ballot after failing the absolute-majority vote on 5 January 2020 (166–165–18).

role_sought: President of the Government (PSOE candidate; head of the Madrid list)
result: PSOE second (121 seats); elected deputy; invested on 16 November 2023
vote_share: 31.7% (PSOE, Congress, 7,821,718 votes); investiture: 179 in favour, 171 against
detail: Snap election called after the PSOE's losses in the May 2023 local and regional elections. Feijóo's investiture failed in September 2023; Sánchez was then re-invested by an absolute majority with the votes of PSOE, Sumar, ERC, Junts, EH Bildu, PNV, BNG and Coalición Canaria, after agreements including an amnesty law.

opponent: Alberto Núñez Feijóo (PP), Santiago Abascal (Vox) and others
detail: Snap election called by Real Decreto 806/2026 of 5 October 2026 (BOE 6 October 2026), about nine months before the end of the legislature, after Congress rejected the government's housing decree-laws on 2 October 2026. Campaign scheduled for 13–27 November 2026.
